newsitem.title: NORWAY: Costs rise at Norway's Aasgard oil/gas field.
newsitem.headline: Costs rise at Norway's Aasgard oil/gas field.

text.p: Development costs at the Aasgard oil and gas field off mid Norway will be almost 15 percent higher than originally estimated, operator Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Wednesday.
The state-owned company said new calculations priced the development at around 30.6 billion crowns compared with the original 26.7 billion crowns.
Statoil said the rise was due to several factors including more equipment and improved environmental measures such as low emission turbines.
"We have raised injection capacity of processed water and gas at the field by 40 percent and gas treatment capacity by 25 percent," spokesman Trygve Skanding said.
Gas treament capacity at Aasgard will be about 15 billion cubic metres per year compared with original plans of 12 billion cubic metres.
Oil and condensate production was increased by 20 percent to 47,000 cubic metres per day (300,000 barrels per day).

Skanding said increased storage capacity for oil on the production ship and extra driling and well installation work also contributed to the rise. But profitability of the project was not affected by the higher costs due to the increased capacity, he said.
Aasgard comprises three fields -- Smoerbukk, Smoerbukk South and Midgard -- in the Norwegian Sea. First oil is scheduled for October 1, 1998 with gas exports expected to begin October 1, 2000.
Partners in Aasgard are Statoil, Mobil Development Norway, Saga Petroleum, Neste Oy, Norsk Agip, Total Norge, Norsk Hydro and Deminex Norge.
